# 14 Execution records and observability

**O-01 — Event envelope.** Each required control event SHALL include event identity, event type, run/object references, object revision or sequence, recorded time, actor, causal/correlation references where applicable, and applicable policy/definition revisions. The runtime SHALL maintain an unambiguous committed order for state transitions of each object; wall-clock timestamps alone SHALL NOT determine causality.

**O-02 — Required events.** The runtime SHALL record admission decisions, plan activations, task creation/delegation, authority decisions and revocations, approval requests and decisions, resource-limit decisions, material capability invocations and outcomes, mission/contract changes, segment changes, waits/resumptions, cancellation, reconciliation, compensation, evidence assessment, acceptance decisions/invalidation, and terminal dispositions. Corrections SHALL append a new event referring to the corrected record.

**O-03 — Decision transparency.** Material decisions SHALL record decision class—deterministic, human, model-mediated, or delegated—together with material input references, applicable rule or configuration, chosen action, and observable justification. Disclosure of hidden chain-of-thought SHALL NOT be required for conformance.

**O-04 — Ledger integrity.** The deployment SHALL protect authoritative control records against unauthorized modification and detect integrity failures using a documented mechanism. Required control records SHALL NOT be sampled away. Telemetry MAY be sampled or exported to OpenTelemetry, but SHALL preserve correlation to the authoritative records where available and SHALL NOT be represented as a complete ledger when incomplete.

**O-05 — Trace correlation.** An observability implementation SHALL provide stable correlations from telemetry to the mission, contract revision, run, node, operation and attempt when applicable. It SHALL distinguish instantaneous control events from measured activity spans, preserve causal references across retries and recovery, and validate incoming trace identifiers. Remote trace context SHALL NOT confer execution authority. Fan-out, joins and asynchronous continuations SHALL retain applicable causal references without implying a temporal parent that did not execute. Telemetry duplication SHALL NOT create a new workflow action.

**O-06 — Operational measurements.** The implementation profile SHALL define metric names, units, populations, aggregation temporality and cardinality limits for execution outcomes, attempts/retries, resource exposure, pending waits, unresolved effects and export health. Where duration is reported, its start/end boundaries and treatment of waiting, retries and clock regression SHALL be stated. Accounting quantities SHALL retain their exact value in authoritative records; a telemetry representation that cannot preserve a value SHALL reject or explicitly mark that measurement rather than silently truncate it. Model token, latency, cost or quality measurements SHALL identify their actual measurement source; absent instrumentation SHALL NOT be represented as zero usage.

**O-07 — Alert governance.** A deployment SHALL define configurable rules, evaluation frequency, accountable recipients, acknowledgement and escalation procedures for stalled execution, overdue approvals, unresolved effects, resource exhaustion and telemetry delivery failures. Alert evaluation SHALL NOT itself grant authority, retry an effect, or resume a wait. Automated remediation SHALL enter through governed commands or triggers, with deduplication and fresh authorization. Operators SHALL monitor failure of the evaluator itself. Deployment assessment SHALL test threshold boundaries, suppressed/duplicate notifications and recovery from an evaluator outage.

**O-08 — Telemetry privacy.** Export SHALL use a declared field allowlist and exclude secrets, credentials, raw prompts, hidden reasoning, action payloads and evidence contents by default. Any broader capture SHALL require an explicit governed policy defining purpose, access, retention and redaction. Hashing identifiers SHALL be described as pseudonymization, not anonymization. The deployment SHALL protect the richer authoritative ledger, restrict exporter endpoints and credentials, apply transport protection appropriate to the environment, and define retention separately for the ledger and telemetry.

**O-09 — Delivery reliability.** A profile claiming durable telemetry SHALL commit its export intent with the authoritative event, use bounded delivery batches and retries, retain observable failure state and define retention and capacity behavior. Network delivery SHALL occur outside the authoritative commit transaction. An exporter failure SHALL NOT be reported as a workflow outcome or cause an external workflow effect to repeat. The profile SHALL state its delivery guarantee and duplicate behavior. For OTLP partial acceptance, the implementation SHALL NOT retry the entire partially accepted batch. Loss, exhausted retries and inability to persist required records SHALL remain visible; failure to persist a required control event SHALL prevent dispatch that depends on it.
